findings.text: The guard does not see the integration tip. The design says test_no_landed_goal_is_pending 'sees the integration tip that the PR would merge into' and that 'CI catches anything that merges later'. But the dev ruleset has strict_required_status_checks_policy false, validate.yml triggers only on pull_request, and ops/merge.py merges on a green rollup. G1021's merge-tree check finds no conflict, because the owner goal never touches docs/design. So G1017 and an owner goal that does not depend on G1017 (the G1020 fallback, or any past-implement goal found at implement) can both pass CI against stale tips and both merge. Dev then holds the landed code and its pending row, and every later PR fails the required check, which its implement cannot fix. Fix: (1) a pending row is allowed only if its owner has 1017 in depends_on, so the first tree with the owner's code and its row is the owner's own PR; (2) a past-implement contract goal that cannot take that dependency gets no row, and instead zzzops edit 1017 adds it to G1017's depends_on, so case 1 applies (G1020 has already integrated, so this costs almost nothing); (3) add a REPAIR line for a red dev; (4) correct the 'sees the integration tip' claim.

G1024 (default-policy update notices, new in Release 1, open, no records, no dependencies) changes the contract but is not in the inventory. It adds a bootstrap provenance record in POLICY.json settings or .zzzops/TEMPLATE.json (SPEC §3.2 and bootstrap), a non-blocking policy_update item in next and validate --policy output (SPEC §3.16 and approval-item rendering), a recorded decline, and a one-time missing-record item. The design's implement-time search for 'DESIGN, SPEC, contract or G1017' does not match G1024's spec, which contains none of them, so the SPEC would drift when G1024 merges. Fix: add G1024 to 'Pending, owner assigned now' the same way as G1022. The root runs zzzops edit 1024 right after approval: depends_on gains 1017, the acceptance line requires the docs/design edit, the HISTORY §4 row and deleting its pending row, and the marker is e.g. plugins/zzzops/zzzops/engine contains "policy_update". Replace the keyword search with a behavioural one: any open goal that changes CLI output, card or approval-item content, policy or settings schema, the template graph, or engine algorithms gets a row and an owner.

findings.text: Nothing checks that SPEC and DESIGN were actually amended. Every test passes when HISTORY §4 has one row per goal in MERGED_AMENDMENTS and SPEC and DESIGN stay at rev 6.3 apart from the scrub and the status lines. That is the cheapest wrong implementation, and its failure is the contract drift this goal removes. Fix: add one sentinel per applied amendment, a contract term the amendment introduces that rev 6.3 lacks, and assert it appears in SPEC.md (or DESIGN.md). I grepped these and all are absent from rev 6.3: #742 `--policy-ref`; G1001 `request_key` or `Request-Key:`; G1014 `inputs_changed`; G1015 `legacy_policy` and `settings.legacy`; G1016 `no_longer_live` or `respond_to`; G1000 `filter_design`; G1020 the 'approved with' notes outcome; G1023's footnote `<full 40-hex sha>`. For G1018 and G1021 pick a term the designer is sure of; `4,096`, `merge-tree` and `CONFLICTING` already appear. Use terms that G1022, G1024, G1025 and G1027 will not remove (no node counts, no engine.min), keyed by goal so a later rename edits one entry.

Nothing checks that the case-3 pending rows exist. Design revision 3 gives G1022 (`plugins/zzzops/zzzops/templates/default/workflow.json lacks "\"truth_design\""`) and G1024 (`plugins/zzzops/zzzops/engine contains "policy_update"`) pending rows, but the tests accept an empty table. An implementation that leaves them out passes, and those goals can then land without the guard ever running on them. Fix: for each of G1022 and G1024, assert that either a pending row exists or HISTORY §4 has a row naming that goal. The second branch keeps the test green after the goal lands and deletes its row. Optionally also assert the row's marker path.

They are stable against later goals: the G1022, G1024 and G1025 designs keep filter_design and shrink and remove none of the others. 1:2: test_known_case_3_goals_are_pending_or_logged requires, for G1022, G1024 and G1025, either a pending row with the expected marker path or a HISTORY section 4 row, and not both, so it stays green after a goal lands and deletes its row. spec:
Dogfooding Release 1 found that DESIGN.md and SPEC.md, the contract that prompts, reviews and goals cite (for example the DESIGN §10 bounded-cost rules and the §5 removal list R1–R15), exist only at /home/dave/Work/dev/zzzops-design-reset/, outside the repository. Workers given only a task card cannot read them through read_dev, and design changes to the contract (G1000, G1015) cannot be reviewed in their PRs.

Outcome:
- The approved revision 6.3 DESIGN.md and SPEC.md move into the repository under docs/design/ (or a path the design chooses), with their review history summarised rather than copied. The passes/ and reviews/ folders stay outside unless the design argues otherwise.
- Every in-repo reference (prompts, skills, references, the implementation plan) points at the in-repo path.
- The documents are updated to the current engine at dev: the --policy-ref flag, and whatever G1001, G1014, G1015, G1016 and G1000 have landed by then, or a short 'pending amendments' list naming those goals.
- A short README section explains which document is normative for what: SPEC is the contract, DESIGN is the rationale.
- Remove anything private: absolute local paths and session names.

Acceptance:
- The documents render on GitHub, and no reference to the external folder remains in shipped files or prompts.
- A card's read_dev can show them.
- The whitepaper goal (G1002) can cite them.
- prompt_stats budgets are unaffected, because these are repository docs and are not shipped in the plugin unless the design decides otherwise.
title: Bring the engine design and spec into the repository as reviewable docs
